newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Navan starts exploration in Bulgaria/Spain.
newsitem.headline: Navan starts exploration in Bulgaria/Spain.

text.p: Navan Resources Plc said on Wednesday that work has started on integrated three-year exploration programmes in both Bulgaria and Spain.

The company said that in 1994/95 it had compiled an in-depth analysis of prospective exploration ground in Bulgaria based upon the experience and knowledge gained in operating the Chelopech gold/copper mine.

Navan said in a statement that it had negotiated and completed the formalisation of a portfolio of exploration and mining licence rights on six targeted licence blocks totalling some 4,500 square kilometres and initial results were highly encouraging.

In Spain during 1995/96, Navan undertook an analysis of various exploration targets in the Spanish pyrite belt predicated around the anticipated successful acquisition of Almagrera SA which owns and operates the Sotiel mining and metallurgical complex near Calanas in southern Spain.

The company said the Almagrera acquisition had now been completed and, as a result, Navan now has an excellent portfolio of highly prospective exploration ground totalling some 170 square kilometres created by the combination of Navan's own exploration licences as well as those acquired with the Almagrera purchase.
"Navan anticipates that over time the Spanish exploration programmes will maximise the return on its recent acquisition," the company said.
Navan also announced the results of the first full year's production at its Chelopech underground gold/copper mine in Bulgaria since the reopening of the mine in early 1995.
Chelopech hoisted and treated 556,000 mt of gold/copper/pyrite bearing ores producing 57,000 ounces of recovered gold and 10.9 million pounds of recovered copper in concentrates last year.

Production continues in 1997 at similar mining and treatment rates but with higher planned average grades, Navan said. Final plans are also being generated for a proposed two or threefold expansion of the operations scheduled to start in early 1998.
Navan said further updates would follow shortly.
